info.name: Internal Intake Agent - Graph Webhook (Task 1)
info.description: Requests to test the Microsoft Graph mailbox-subscription webhook (validation handshake + notification handling) and the admin bootstrap/status endpoints. Set the `baseUrl` collection variable to your local dev server (e.g. http://localhost:8000) or production (https://complaint-back.azurewebsites.net) depending on what you're testing.

request.description: Simulates the handshake Graph performs when a subscription is created/renewed. Expected: 200 OK, body is exactly 'hello123', Content-Type: text/plain.

Simulates a real Graph new-mail notification. Expected: 202 Accepted. Check server logs for 'new message test-message-id-123' — actual fetch/classify/ingest isn't wired yet (task 2/3), this only proves routing + clientState validation work.

Expected: still 202 overall (Graph shouldn't get an error and retry-storm you), but check server logs for 'unrecognized clientState — dropping notification' and confirm NO 'new message' log line appears for this one.

exec: pm.test('Status is 202 (silently dropped, not an error)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(202));

request.description: ONE-TIME action. Only run this against a host whose GRAPH_NOTIFICATION_URL is correct and publicly reachable, and only after the Exchange Application Access Policy is confirmed working (step 3 of test_graph_intake_setup.py passes). Expected: 200 with subscription_id + expires_at. 503 = Graph not configured. 502 = Graph rejected the request (check notification URL / permissions).
Read-only. Shows tracked subscriptions with status/expiry/last_error. Safe to call any time.
